prerequisites: Mastery of material and energy balances in multicomponent systems with and without chemical reaction, as studied in the 'Fundamentals of Chemical Processes' course.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of material and energy balances, biotechnology, mass transfer, separation operations, chemical reaction engineering, reactor design, and valorization and transformation of raw materials and energy resources.
Ability for analysis, design, simulation, and optimization of processes and products.

Ability to design and manage applied experimentation procedures, especially for the determination of thermodynamic and transport properties, and modeling of phenomena and systems in the field of chemical engineering, fluid flow systems, heat transmission, mass transfer operations, chemical reaction kinetics, and reactors.
Obtain, interpret, and model kinetic data for homogeneous and heterogeneous reactions, mastering the basic theory of chemical kinetics and catalysis.
Select and design ideal isothermal reactors to carry out simple reactions.
Perform energy balances for ideal chemical reactors, design adiabatic reactors, and conduct stability studies of reactors for simple cases (CSTR).
Identify non-ideality phenomena in real reactors, modeling them using simple systematic approaches.
Understand the fundamentals of operating heterogeneous reactors.

syllabus_topics: Integral method for kinetic data analysis
Differential method for kinetic data analysis
Selection of reactor type and optimal reactor arrangement for simple reactions
Selection of reactor type and optimal reactor arrangement for multiple reactions
Resolution of energy balances. Analytical design methods
Thermal stability in reactors. Multiplicity of steady states
Thermal stability in continuous stirred-tank reactors. Heat balances
Kinetics of heterogeneous reactions. General concepts
Unreacted core model for spherical particles of constant size
Unreacted core model for spherical particles of decreasing size
Nature and characterization of solid catalysts
Characteristics and properties of solid catalysts
Kinetics of solid-catalyzed reactions: diffusional resistance in pores
The effectiveness factor. Definition and estimation
Kinetics in the presence of external diffusion
General concepts of Fluid-Fluid reaction kinetics
assessment_rules: For both ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade is composed of 20% from Group Tutorials and 80% from the final exam. Attendance to Group Tutorials is mandatory, with valid attendance being above 80% in justified cases. The final exam consists of theoretical/practical questions (50% of exam grade) and problem solving (50% of exam grade); to pass, a minimum of 30% must be obtained in both parts of the final exam. For the December-January call, the final exam grade cannot be less than 40% of its maximum value. For students under differentiated evaluation, the final exam accounts for 100% of the grade.
